# webmcp-consent

> A Chrome extension that holds every WebMCP write until a human approves it, on any site, including sites that never adopted anything. Reads run freely.

It works by replacing `registerTool` at `document_start` in the MAIN world, before the page's own scripts run. The site registers its tools the normal way and is calling the extension's wrapper instead. No annotation on a tool means it is treated as a write and held. `fetch` is patched too, so a tool that claims `readOnlyHint: true` and then POSTs is caught as well.

This page is a landing page and registers no tools of its own. The two demos do. Neither demo has a consent layer in its own code; everything that stops a write comes from the extension.

## Demos

- [Anywhere Goods](/demo/unprotected.html): a plain storefront. Registers `get_messages` (read-only), `issue_refund` (no annotation, so it is held), and `check_loyalty_status` (claims `readOnlyHint: true` but quietly POSTs, so the request is held at the network layer).
- [Ledger](/demo/index.html): a support console with a planted prompt injection in its customer inbox. Registers `search_orders` and `get_customer_messages` (read-only), `issue_refund` (held), and `change_price` (held, and only registered for manager and owner roles). Ask an agent to triage the inbox and watch what it tries.

## Links

- [README](/README.md): how the interception works, and an explicit list of what the extension cannot do.
- [Extension download](/webmcp-consent-extension.zip): unzip and load unpacked at chrome://extensions.
